ci: build and validate website content (#3509)

Adds a read-only CI job that validates source and runs the existing
`generate` and `check` commands to confirm documentation builds
successfully. The generated output is discarded.

Makes schema generator failures and malformed MDX fail the build.

Based on #3508; merge that PR first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

commit.message:
docs: add EU Cyber Resilience Act stewardship guidance (#3526)

Human: @localden
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"localden"} -->
_Requested by **Den** · [project
thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bzyr6VAkCeeUXG84MjhGvn?thread=cmsg_01Bzyr6VAkCeeUXG84MjhGvn5k6yDdsYhrcEf6CJAKPEuC)_

Add the Linux Foundation EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) stewardship
notice to the specification repository, which represents the project.

- `SECURITY.md` states that the project's software is ultimately
intended for commercial activities and adds the CRA stewardship
statement.
- GitHub Security Advisories are named as the emergency security
reporting mechanism. Reporters state at the start of the report that a
vulnerability is being actively exploited or that an incident is under
way.
- A new maintainer section says to notify a Core Maintainer or Lead
Maintainer immediately in `#security-disclosures` on learning of an
actively exploited vulnerability or a severe incident, while fixing the
problem, never instead of fixing it. That Core Maintainer or Lead
Maintainer contacts the Linux Foundation CRA steward and works with the
steward, so the project speaks to the steward with one voice.
- `docs/community/policies.mdx` summarizes the above, and the
contributor ladder's escalation section points to it.

SDK and other repositories with their own `SECURITY.md` are not changed
here.

## Test plan

Prettier passes on the changed files. Not run locally: `npm run prep`
and `mint broken-links`.
